short: The lead ship of her class, USS Yorktown was instrumental in halting Japanese expansion at the Coral Sea and Midway.
full:
Commissioned in 1937, USS Yorktown was designed to maximize aircraft capacity and speed within the restrictions of interwar naval treaties. She served in the Atlantic before rapidly transferring to the Pacific following Pearl Harbor. At the Battle of the Coral Sea in May 1942, she suffered severe damage but miraculously returned to Pearl Harbor, where repair crews patched her up in just three days.

Yorktown immediately sailed to join the ambush at the Battle of Midway in June 1942. Her aircraft helped destroy the Japanese carrier strike force, but Yorktown became the primary target of Japanese retaliation. Disabled by dive bombers and torpedo planes, she was finally sunk by a Japanese submarine while under tow, giving her life to secure a pivotal American victory.
